proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(K_a=K_a(n_T)\), \(J_a=K_a(k_T)\), \(\sigma_a^2=\operatorname{Var}_P(X_{a,1}^{\Delta})\), and
\[
 Z_T=(M_{1,\Delta}-PM_{1,\Delta})-(M_{0,\Delta}-PM_{0,\Delta}),
 \qquad
 C_T=(U_{1,\Delta}-PU_{1,\Delta})-(U_{0,\Delta}-PU_{0,\Delta}).
\]
The arm-tape equivalence and the old-cohort correction lemma give, on \(E_T\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}=Z_T+C_T. \tag{1}
\]
This identity is unconditional in the tape variables; the event \(E_T\) only determines whether the observable estimator uses the displayed deterministic prefixes.

The delay envelope also excludes genuinely infinite delays. Indeed, the events \(\{D(a)>u\}\) decrease to \(\{D(a)=\infty\}\) as the integer \(u\) tends to infinity, and continuity from above gives
\[
 P\{D(a)=\infty\}=\lim_{u\to\infty}P\{D(a)>u\}
 \leq\lim_{u\to\infty}L(1+u)^{-\beta}=0.
\]

We first verify measurability. On \(E_T\), the first \(K_a\) assignments to arm \(a\) occur by \(n_T\), so at time \(H_T\) their ages are at least
\[
 H_T-n_T=m_T+\Delta_T=g_{T,\Delta}.
\]
The first \(J_a\) assignments occur by \(k_T\), so their ages are at least
\[
 H_T-k_T=h_{T,\Delta}.
\]
If such a response has appeared, \(O_{T,\Delta}\) records its outcome and delay; if it has not appeared by \(H_T\), its delay exceeds the relevant guaranteed age and the corresponding truncated indicator is zero. Thus every \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), \(R_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), sample variance, gate, and interval endpoint is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable. The conventions on \(E_T^c\) are measurable as well.

We next prove finite-sample coverage of the concentration branch. If \(X\in[-1,1]\), convexity of the exponential on this interval gives
\[
 P\exp\{\lambda(X-PX)\}\leq \exp(\lambda^2/2).
\]
Multiplication over the independent tape entries, followed by exponential Markov inequality and optimization in \(\lambda\), therefore yields
\[
 P\{|Z_T|>\sqrt{2S_Tx}\}\leq2e^{-x},
 \qquad S_T=K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]
For \(R=Y\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\), bounded outcomes and the delay envelope imply
\[
 |R-PR|\leq2,
 \qquad P(R-PR)^2\leq PR^2\leq v_{T,\Delta}.
\]
For every integer \(j\geq2\), \(|R-PR|^j\leq2^{j-2}(R-PR)^2\). Expanding the exponential series, applying exponential Markov inequality to the \(J_a\) independent terms, and optimizing gives
\[
 P\!\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-PU_{a,\Delta}|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}. \tag{3}
\]
Take \(x=x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\). The union of the three exceptional events in (2)--(3) has probability at most \(\eta\). On its complement, (1), the triangle inequality, and \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\) show that \(\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) whenever \(E_T\) holds. Intersecting with \([-2,2]\) cannot remove \(\tau\), and on \(E_T^c\) the reported interval is \([-2,2]\). Hence this coverage argument never conditions on quota success.

It remains to justify the Gaussian branch and the data-dependent splice. Define the deterministic, law-dependent variance quantity
\[
 V_T=\sigma_1^2+\mathbf 1\{\alpha=0\}\sigma_0^2.
\]
First consider any triangular array for which \(V_T\geq1/\log T\). If \(\alpha>0\), then
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq\frac{1}{K_1\log T};
\]
if \(\alpha=0\), the quota orders give \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq c_0/(T\log T)\) for a constant \(c_0>0\). Write \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}=\sum_j\xi_{Tj}\) using its independent centered tape summands. Their variances sum to one, while the largest absolute summand is bounded by
\[
 \delta_T:=\max_j|\xi_{Tj}|
 =O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{K_1}}\right)=o(1)
\]
when \(\alpha>0\), and by \(O(\sqrt{\log T/T})=o(1)\) when \(\alpha=0\). For fixed \(u\), Taylor expansion with the deterministic bound \(|\xi_{Tj}|\leq\delta_T\) gives
\[
 P e^{iu\xi_{Tj}}
 =1-\frac{u^2}{2}P\xi_{Tj}^2
 +O\bigl(|u|^3\delta_TP\xi_{Tj}^2\bigr).
\]
Taking logarithms and using
\(\sum_j(P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2\leq\delta_T^2\sum_jP\xi_{Tj}^2=\delta_T^2\), we obtain
\[
 \prod_jPe^{iu\xi_{Tj}}
 =\exp\{-u^2/2+o(1)\}. \tag{4}
\]
The unit second moment gives tightness, and (4) identifies every subsequential limit with the standard Gaussian law. Since the bounds on \(\delta_T\) are uniform and the Gaussian distribution function is continuous, the usual contradiction-subsequence argument gives
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}\sup_x
 \left|P\{Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0 \tag{5}
\]
uniformly over this variance regime.

The correction is negligible without any independence between it and \(Z_T\). By the old-cohort correction lemma and the quota orders,
\[
 PC_T^2\leq C_1T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{PC_T^2}{s_{T,\Delta}^2}
 \leq C_2(\log T)T^{1-\alpha-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\longrightarrow0, \tag{6}
\]
because \(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\).

For a sample of size \(K\geq2\), the usual sample variance satisfies
\[
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{K}{K-1}\{\overline{X^2}-\bar X^2\}.
\]
Since \(|X|\leq1\), Chebyshev's inequality applied separately to \(\overline{X^2}\) and \(\bar X\) yields, uniformly in the law,
\[
 \widehat\sigma_a^2-\sigma_a^2=O_P(K_a^{-1/2}). \tag{7}
\]
When \(\alpha>0\), division of the arm-one contribution by \(s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq1/(K_1\log T)\) gives \(O_P(\log T/\sqrt{K_1})=o_P(1)\), and the relative arm-zero error is at most
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{K_1\log T}{K_0^{3/2}}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
When \(\alpha=0\), both quotas are comparable to \(T\), so division by the lower bound \(c_0/(T\log T)\) again gives \(o_P(1)\). Thus
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow1 \tag{8}
\]
uniformly whenever \(V_T\geq1/\log T\). Equations (1), (5), (6), (8), and \(P(E_T^c)\leq4T^{-4}\) prove the uniform studentized approximation in that regime, after assigning an arbitrary fixed value to the quotient on \(E_T^c\).

The regular class lies in this regime eventually. Indeed, with \(X=Y\mathbf 1\{D\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\), boundedness gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\operatorname{Var}(X)-\operatorname{Var}(Y)|
 &\leq |P(X^2-Y^2)|+|(PX)^2-(PY)^2|\\
 &\leq3P\{D>g_{T,\Delta}\}
 \leq3v_{T,\Delta}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Because \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\to\infty\), the last quantity tends to zero uniformly. The regular-variance assumption therefore gives \(V_T\geq\kappa/2\) eventually, with the same conclusion after summing the two errors when \(\alpha=0\). This proves both studentization assertions on \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\).

For coverage of the Gaussian branch, set
\[
 f_B(s)=s c_\eta(B/s),\qquad s>0.
\]
If \(Z\) is standard normal, the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) and monotonicity in the absolute shift imply, for every \(|b|\leq B\),
\[
 P\{|sZ-b|\leq f_B(s)\}
 =\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)+b/s)+\Phi(c_\eta(B/s)-b/s)-1
 \geq1-\eta. \tag{10}
\]
Writing \(x=c_\eta(u)-u\), the defining equation gives
\[
 z_{1-\eta}\leq x\leq z_{1-\eta/2},
 \qquad
 B+z_{1-\eta}s\leq f_B(s)\leq B+z_{1-\eta/2}s. \tag{11}
\]
Implicit differentiation gives
\[
 c_\eta'(u)=
 \frac{\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)-\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 {\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)+\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}\in[0,1].
\]
Hence
\[
 f_B'(s)=x+
 \frac{2u\phi(x+2u)}{\phi(x)+\phi(x+2u)},
\]
which is bounded uniformly in \(B\geq0\) and \(s>0\), because \(x\geq z_{1-\eta}>0\) and \(u e^{-2u x-2u^2}\) is bounded. Thus (5)--(8), (10), and a deterministic endpoint sandwich give coverage at least \(1-\eta-o(1)\) for \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\), uniformly over \(V_T\geq1/\log T\). The nonnegative radius \(d_{T,\Delta}\) only enlarges the interval. Moreover, the quota orders and the two strict inequalities in the definition of \(\rho\) give
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}
 =O\!\left(
 \sqrt{T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\log T}
 +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\log T\right)
 =o(T^{-q}). \tag{12}
\]

Finally we check the observable splice. If \(V_T\leq1/\log T\), (7), Chebyshev's inequality, and \((\log T)^2/K_1\to0\) imply
\[
 \sup_{P,\Pi}P(G_{T,\Delta})\longrightarrow0. \tag{13}
\]
The selected interval then differs from the concentration interval with vanishing probability, so (2)--(3) give coverage at least \(1-\eta-o(1)\). If \(V_T>1/\log T\), then on \(G_{T,\Delta}^c\), bounded sample variances and the definition of the gate imply
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q}):
\]
for \(\alpha>0\), \(\widehat s^2\leq2/(K_1\log T)+2/K_0\), while for \(\alpha=0\), \(\widehat s^2=O(1/(T\log T))\). By (11)--(12),
\[
 f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+o(T^{-q}).
\]
On the other hand \(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\asymp T^{-q}\), so, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the concentration interval contains the Gaussian interval on gate failure. On gate success the selected interval is the Gaussian interval itself. Thus in the high-variance regime the selected interval contains a uniformly valid Gaussian interval, and in the low-variance regime it selects the concentration fallback except on an event of probability \(o(1)\). Together with the full interval on \(E_T^c\), this proves uniform honesty over both declared model classes. Every bound used only the deterministic propensity envelopes through the quota orders, so no limit of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\) was assumed.

Uniform coverage is the conclusion of the uniform gated-inference theorem. We prove the length bound branch by branch. The quota-success lemma gives
\[
 S_T=K_1(n_T)^{-1}+K_0(n_T)^{-1}=O(T^{-(1-\alpha)}),
 \qquad a_T=O(T^{-q}). \tag{14}
\]
The delay envelope, the quota orders, and \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\asymp T^\rho\) give, for fixed \(x_\eta\),
\[
 A_{1,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)+A_{0,T,\Delta}(x_\eta)
 =O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)/2}+T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\right)
 =o(T^{-q}), \tag{15}
\]
where the last equality uses \(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\) and \(\rho>1/2\). The same calculation with \(4\log T\) gives \(d_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q})\). A sample variance of variables in \([-1,1]\) is bounded by a universal constant, hence \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-q})\). Inequality (11) from the proof of the gated theorem yields
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_{T,\Delta}. \tag{16}
\]
Since \(h_{T,\Delta}=H_T-k_T\) and \(k_T/H_T\leq T^{\rho-1}\to0\), uniformly over deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\),
\[
 B_{T,\Delta}=O((1+H_T)^{-\beta}). \tag{17}
\]
Equations (14)--(17) show that both interval branches have length at most a constant multiple of
\(r_{T,\Delta}=\max\{T^{-q},(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}\) on \(E_T\). On \(E_T^c\) the length is four, and the quota-success lemma bounds its expected contribution by \(16T^{-4}=o(r_{T,\Delta})\). This proves the uniform expected-length upper bound.

For the sampling lower bound, fix one deterministic policy in every paired experiment:
\[
 \pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha},\qquad \pi_t(0)=1-ct^{-\alpha}.
\]
It belongs to \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\), because \(c\leq C\), \(ct^{-\alpha}\leq c\leq1-\varepsilon\), and the current assignment is independent of the current potential vector. Put all delays equal to zero and make arm zero identically zero. Under \(P_+\) and \(P_-\), let the arm-one outcome be Rademacher with respective means \(d_T\) and \(-d_T\), where
\[
 Q_T=\sum_{t\leq T}ct^{-\alpha},
 \qquad d_T=\lambda Q_T^{-1/2},
\]
and \(\lambda>0\) is fixed and small. The one-observation Hellinger affinity of these two Rademacher laws is \(\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\). Since the assignment law is common, independence over recruitment times gives affinity
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal A_T
 &=\prod_{t\leq T}\left[1-ct^{-\alpha}\{1-\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\}\right]\\
 &\geq1-\sum_{t\leq T}ct^{-\alpha}d_T^2
 =1-\lambda^2. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{18}
\]
For densities \(p,q\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives directly
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \leq\sqrt{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pq}\right)^2}.
\]
Thus the total variation distance between the two logged experiments is at most \(\sqrt2\lambda\). Their causal contrasts are \(d_T\) and \(-d_T\). If an interval \(J_{T,\Delta}\) has the asserted uniform coverage, then under \(P_+\) it contains both points with probability at least \(1-2\eta-\sqrt2\lambda-o(1)\). Choose \(\lambda<(1-2\eta)/\sqrt2\). Since \(Q_T\asymp T^{1-\alpha}\),
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq2d_T\{1-2\eta-\sqrt2\lambda-o(1)\}
 \geq c_{\eta,1}T^{-q}. \tag{19}
\]

For the hidden-tail lower bound, retain this same policy and set
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}.
\]
In each arm put mass \(1-\delta_T\) at \((Y,D)=(0,0)\) and mass \(\delta_T\) at delay \(H_T+1\). Under \(P_+\), the delayed outcomes are \(+1\) in arm one and \(-1\) in arm zero; under \(P_-\), reverse both signs. For every integer \(u\leq H_T\),
\[
 P\{D>u\}=\delta_T\leq L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\leq L(1+u)^{-\beta},
\]
and for \(u\geq H_T+1\) this tail probability is zero. Thus the delay envelope holds, all delays are finite, and boundedness holds. No delayed atom is visible by \(H_T\), so the two complete observed experiments, including their missingness patterns, assignments, and logged propensities, have exactly the same law. Their causal contrasts are \(2\delta_T\) and \(-2\delta_T\). Under the common observed law, the interval contains both points with probability at least \(1-2\eta-o(1)\); therefore
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T}E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq4\delta_T\{1-2\eta-o(1)\}
 \geq c_{\eta,2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta}. \tag{20}
\]
Taking the larger of (19) and (20) proves the stated lower bound by a fixed multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\). When \(\Delta_T=0\), \(H_T=T\), giving \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\).

The already established one-sided minimax-length theorem applies to exactly \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\) and to the same deterministic quotas and interval. Its first two displays state respectively
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1)
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 E_{P,\Pi}|I_{T,\Delta}|\leq C_\eta r_{T,\Delta}.
\]
These are precisely the two assertions of the corrected proposition. In particular, its achievability conclusion uses the arm-one lower allocation envelope and the control floor through the deterministic quota orders; no upper allocation envelope is used.

Let \(Z\sim N(0,1)\). For \(c>0\) and \(v\geq0\),
\[
 P\{|Z-v|\leq c\}=\Phi(c-v)+\Phi(c+v)-1. \tag{21}
\]
The derivative of the right side in \(v\) is \(\phi(c+v)-\phi(c-v)\leq0\). Hence the least coverage over shifts of absolute value at most \(u\) occurs at the endpoint \(u\). For fixed \(u\), the right side of (21) is continuous and strictly increasing in \(c\), from zero to one. This proves existence and uniqueness of \(c_\eta(u)\), and its defining equation gives exact coverage \(1-\eta\) at the endpoint shift.

Now suppose \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q\). On the regular class, the variance comparison (9) in the gated-inference proof and the regular-variance assumption imply
\[
 0<c_0T^{-2q}\leq s_{T,0}^2\leq C_0T^{-2q} \tag{22}
\]
uniformly. The old-cohort correction lemma gives \(B_{T,0}=O(T^{-q})\), so \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\) is uniformly bounded. Uniform studentization, \(\widehat s_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to1\), the uniform Lipschitz property of \(f_B(s)=s c_\eta(B/s)\) established in the gated-inference proof, and \(|b_{T,0}|\leq B_{T,0}\) imply from (21) that
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).
\]
The added radius \(d_{T,0}=o(T^{-q})=o(s_{T,0})\) is nonnegative and does not change the limiting endpoint calibration.

We construct an attaining triangular family. Use the deterministic policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\) and put
\[
 \delta_T=L(1+T)^{-q}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\), so that \(\delta_T<1/2\). Index the two alternatives by \(\zeta\in\{-1,1\}\). In arm one, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(-\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\). In arm zero, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,-\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\). The two arms may be taken independent within each arrival vector, and the vectors are independent and identically distributed over recruitment times.

These laws have bounded outcomes and finite delays. For integer \(u\leq T\), their delay tail is \(\delta_T\leq L(1+u)^{-q}\), and it is zero for \(u\geq T+1\), so the polynomial envelope holds without outcome--delay independence. In each arm the visible and hidden means cancel, while \(Y^2=1\); hence
\[
 PY(1)=PY(0)=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P(Y(1))=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(0))=1. \tag{23}
\]
Thus the family is in the regular class whenever its variance floor is support-feasible, namely \(\kappa\leq1\) for \(\alpha>0\) and \(\kappa\leq2\) for \(\alpha=0\); for larger \(\kappa\) that regular class is empty by bounded support.

Because \(g_{T,0}<h_{T,0}<T+1\), every correction variable is zero. For \(\zeta=1\),
\[
 \tau=0,
 \qquad b_{T,0}=2\delta_T,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(X_{a,1}^{0})=1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2,
\]
and therefore
\[
 s_{T,0}^2=(1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2)(K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}). \tag{24}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \frac{b_{T,0}}{B_{T,0}}
 =\left(\frac{1+h_{T,0}}{1+T}\right)^q\longrightarrow1. \tag{25}
\]
The quota asymptotics in (24) now yield
\[
 \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u=
 \begin{cases}
 2L\sqrt{c/(1-\alpha)},&\alpha>0,\\
 2L(c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1})^{-1/2},&\alpha=0,
 \end{cases} \tag{26}
\]
which is finite and strictly positive. The bounded independent triangular-array calculation used in (4), together with quota success and sample-variance consistency, gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau+b_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
 \qquad \frac{\widehat s_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Combining this with (25)--(26) proves
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(-u,1),
 \qquad \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u.
\]
Since \(\tau=0\) is in the interior of \([-2,2]\) and all radii vanish, truncation at the parameter-space boundary is asymptotically irrelevant. Thus for every fixed \(c'>0\),
\[
 P\{\tau\in[\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\}
 \longrightarrow \Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1.
\]
By (21), \(c'=c_\eta(u)\) gives equality \(1-\eta\), and every smaller symmetric critical value gives strictly smaller endpoint-shift coverage. This proves attainment in the delayed adaptive experiment.

A stationary binary endpoint takes values in \([0,1]\subset[-1,1]\), and its risk difference is the causal contrast \(\tau=PY(1)-PY(0)\). Once the logged inferior-arm probabilities satisfy the two-sided rare-arm envelope and the ascertainment delays satisfy the polynomial envelope, the trial law belongs to the informative-delay model class. If
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\not\longrightarrow0,
\]
the hidden-sign construction in the Wald frontier, with any fixed support-feasible variance floor, is a subfamily of this model class and disproves uniform honesty of the unpadded interval. This proves the proposition's class-wide necessary condition. In contrast, the uniform gated-inference theorem supplies the bias-aware Gaussian branch and concentration fallback from the same terminal records without a regular-variance premise, so either such a pad-and-fallback rule or additional prespecified follow-up is required for a class-wide guarantee when the displayed tail obstruction remains.

If the regular-variance condition is independently verified, the sufficiency half of the Wald frontier shows that the displayed product tending to zero is also sufficient for the ordinary interval. Without that variance condition, the Gaussian branch is used only behind the observable gate in \(I_{T,\Delta}\); the concentration branch alone is also valid by (2)--(3). Thus the corrected protocol rule does not silently apply a studentized Gaussian approximation in a degenerate regime.

The follow-up condition has the following explicit elbow. Since \(q=(1-\alpha)/2>0\),
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\to0
\]
holds with \(\Delta_T=0\) whenever \(\beta>q\). If \(\beta=q\), it is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\Delta_T}{T}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
If \(\beta<q\), it is equivalent to
\[
 T+\Delta_T\gg T^{q/\beta}.
\]
Finally, this is a uniform statement over the envelope class. At a particular prompt-delay law the hidden bias is zero, so the construction does not imply pointwise Wald failure there.

Assume \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms. Since \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) and \(h_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), the definitions give
\[
 X_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j},
 \qquad R_{a,j}^{\Delta}=0,
 \qquad U_{a,\Delta}=0.
\]
Moreover \(\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}=0\), and hence \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\). On quota success,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=M_{1,\Delta}-M_{0,\Delta},
\]
a difference of two independent deterministic-prefix arm-tape means. On the regular class, the maximal normalized summand tends to zero by the quota orders and the variance floor. The characteristic-function calculation (4) and the sample-variance calculation (7)--(8) therefore give pointwise standard-normal studentization. Since quota failure has probability at most \(4T^{-4}\) and returns the full parameter interval, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest for this prompt-delay law.

The generic radius \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is a worst-case radius for the whole polynomial envelope; because \(L>0\), it need not vanish merely because the particular law has prompt delays. Continuity and strict monotonicity in the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) give
\[
 c_\eta(u)\longrightarrow c_\eta(0)=z_{1-\eta/2}
 \qquad\text{as }u\downarrow0.
\]
Thus, if \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\), the random critical value converges to the ordinary-Wald critical value. On a regular prompt-delay sequence, (12), (22), and variance consistency also give
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Conversely, if \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\) does not tend to zero, a subsequence stays bounded away from zero, and strict monotonicity gives a critical value bounded away from \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) on a further subsequence. Hence the generic Gaussian branch reduces to ordinary Wald asymptotically exactly under the displayed bias-ratio condition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable and uniformly honest over \(\mathfrak M_T(\alpha,\beta,L,c,C,\varepsilon)\cup\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), without conditioning on \(E_T\) and without convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\). Measurability follows from the recorded calendar revelation times, including when a response remains unrevealed at \(H_T\). On \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), assign the displayed studentized quotient the value zero on \(E_T^c\). Then \(\sup_x|P\{(\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta})/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)|\to0\) and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\) uniformly.
